title: A pre-emptive vaccine against diverse pandemic coronaviruses

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a vaccine that provides durable protection against substantially different coronaviruses before a new pandemic threat emerges. Its defining capability would be protection extending beyond the viruses used to design it, including genuinely divergent threats. This is a target capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

Scientific framing from the research notes: coronavirus spike variation makes breadth difficult, while antibody targets shared across viruses may be hard to expose or make dominant in the immune response. The intended vaccine would need to turn recognition of shared features into reliable protection across diverse threats. These are proposed scientific motivations; the retained source copies contain no scientific text with which to verify the specific mechanisms.

Conceptual distinction: breadth must be defined by both the viruses covered and the outcome protected against. Preventing severe disease, preventing symptomatic illness and preventing infection or onward transmission are different capabilities. The concept does not require assuming that success on one endpoint automatically establishes the others, or that coverage of selected coronavirus lineages establishes coverage of the entire family.

significance.text: Conditional impact: if a sufficiently broad and durable vaccine were deployed before a divergent coronavirus emerged, vaccinated people could enter the outbreak with useful protection already in place. This would change preparedness from relying entirely on a vaccine developed after identification to having some protection available at the beginning. The revolutionary element is advance protection against unfamiliar threats.

Conditional downstream possibilities depend on the protection achieved. Protection against severe disease could reduce clinical burden even if infections continued. Substantial protection against infection or transmission could also help constrain spread. These possibilities require separate evidence: broad neutralization alone would not establish either population-level outcome.

Limits on impact: a vaccine's availability would not create immediate population immunity. Benefits would depend on prior deployment, uptake, delivery, durability and effectiveness in the people exposed. Even successful coverage of a diverse test panel would not guarantee protection against every future coronavirus or establish that pandemics would be prevented. Pre-emptive breadth and rapid responses to newly identified threats would remain complementary capabilities.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target breakthrough is a reproducible way to elicit a durable protective immune response across known and genuinely divergent coronavirus threats. The supplied evidence does not establish how close the field is to this capability or whether it remains unachieved across all relevant approaches as of November 2026. That uncertainty concerns the state of the evidence, while the innovation's intended capability remains clear.

Proposed scientific barriers include selecting shared targets that remain useful across divergent viruses, presenting those targets so they reliably attract protective responses, and sustaining those responses over time. The research specifically identifies spike variation, conserved-target accessibility and immunological dominance as obstacles. Their importance in the particular reported vaccine approach cannot be verified from the retained copies.

Scientific reasoning: isolating an antibody with cross-lineage activity would demonstrate that a particular antibody can recognize and neutralize the tested viruses. It would not by itself demonstrate that vaccination regularly produces enough of that activity in the overall immune response, that the response persists, or that it protects an animal or person. Bridging those levels—from isolated antibodies to consistent serum activity to durable protection—is a central evidentiary and engineering requirement.

Proposed development barriers also include choosing a virus panel that meaningfully tests generalization, using appropriate protection models, and establishing safety and effectiveness across intended human populations. A panel concentrated around the design viruses could overstate breadth. Conversely, success against selected divergent viruses would establish useful demonstrated breadth without resolving performance against every untested threat.

current_state.text: The research notes attribute a nonhuman-primate study to Dueker and colleagues under the title “Heterologous betacoronavirus spike immunization in non-human primates elicits antibodies that neutralize both sarbeco- and merbecoviruses,” with a reported Cell Reports publication date of 3 June 2026 and DOI 10.1016/j.celrep.2026.117439. Those bibliographic details are carried forward as research-note attributions. The supplied review could not verify the document identity or publication details from the retained PubMed copy.

The same notes report rare isolated antibodies with cross-lineage neutralization following nonhuman-primate immunization, while describing the serum response as insufficient to establish broadly protective immunity. An earlier research pass additionally reported undetectable S2-directed serum cross-neutralization. Neither retained source contains scientific content substantiating antibody rarity, neutralization breadth, serum findings or S2 specificity. These remain reported findings requiring verification; the access failure does not show that they are false.

The research described the second PubMed item as a separate January 2026 preprint and stated that its abstract had been inspected. The supplied review found only a cookie-access notice in that retained copy, just as in the purported published record. Consequently, the retained evidence does not establish the second item's identity, date, preprint status or relationship to the reported publication. The earlier claim of an inspectable preprint abstract cannot be retained as a verified account of the available material.

Both retained PubMed artifacts were retrieved on 11 November 2026 and contain access notices rather than abstracts or full scientific text. The source index records saved, untruncated artifacts, but successful saving does not establish access to article content. No independently inspected published full text, verified quantitative performance results or demonstrated human protection can be established from these copies. The empty freshness record also leaves completeness of coverage through 1 November 2026 unresolved; retrieval on 11 November does not establish that the research was current.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: human trials would establish an acceptable safety profile and durable protection against multiple circulating coronaviruses, using explicit clinical endpoints and a prespecified follow-up period. The development program would state whether its claim concerns severe disease, symptomatic illness, infection or transmission. These are proposed criteria for convincing evidence, not an established consensus standard; the supplied materials specify no justified numerical efficacy threshold or duration.
completion_criteria.label: Human trials establish acceptable safety and durable multi-coronavirus protection

completion_criteria.text: Proposed breadth demonstration: neutralization studies and appropriate animal-protection experiments would test a diverse, prespecified set of viruses excluded from vaccine design. Selection would explain which coronavirus lineages and degrees of divergence are represented and how exclusion tests generalization. Results would distinguish isolated antibody activity, serum neutralization and protection after challenge, with assay conditions and limitations made explicit.
completion_criteria.label: Breadth experiments demonstrate protection against prespecified viruses excluded from vaccine-design

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirement: independent laboratories would reproduce the central breadth findings, and further cohorts would show that protective responses occur consistently rather than only in exceptional individuals. Follow-up would assess persistence and the effect of additional doses. A credible interpretation would disclose unsuccessful tests and specify the populations, viruses, endpoints and observation periods for which protection was demonstrated.
completion_criteria.label: Independently reproduced breadth findings accompany consistent protective responses across cohorts

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: the vaccine would need a feasible manufacturing and delivery regimen compatible with deployment before an outbreak. Evidence would identify any dependence on boosting and any limits in intended recipient groups. No finite experimental program could prove literal protection against every future coronavirus; completion would mean a clearly bounded, reproducible demonstration of broad and durable protection.
completion_criteria.label: Feasible manufacturing and delivery enable deployment before an outbreak

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: INF-09, “A rapid, end-to-end vaccine response to a newly identified pathogen,” addresses speed after identification, whereas INF-08 addresses breadth established before emergence. They could reinforce one another if a pre-emptive vaccine supplied initial protection while a tailored response was developed. The supplied roster supports this title-level distinction, although no fuller INF-09 definition or evidence record is available here.

Roster-based comparison: INF-01, “A broadly protective HIV vaccine,” shares the ambition of protection despite viral diversity. INF-03, “A tuberculosis vaccine that interrupts transmission,” and INF-13, “A highly protective, durable and readily deliverable malaria vaccine,” overlap in vaccination, durability or deployment goals. Their pathogens and intended protection endpoints remain distinct; success in one would not establish success in another.

Roster-based comparison: INF-07, “Broad-spectrum treatment for unrelated viral infections,” also seeks breadth, but concerns treatment across unrelated viruses rather than pre-emptive vaccination within coronaviruses. INF-02, “A safe, scalable cure for established HIV infection,” INF-11, “A safe, broadly effective treatment-free cure for chronic hepatitis B,” and INF-12, “Very short, reliable curative treatment for active and latent tuberculosis,” concern curing established infections rather than supplying advance vaccine protection.

Roster-based comparison: INF-10, “Prevention of multiple sclerosis by controlling Epstein–Barr virus,” and INF-14, “Mechanism-guided prevention of major post-viral syndromes,” concern downstream consequences of viral infection. INF-08 could contribute to preventing such consequences only where its protection and the relevant disease pathway were demonstrated. Protection against acute coronavirus disease alone would not establish prevention of a post-viral syndrome.

Roster-based comparison: INF-04, “A reliable way to break malaria transmission through its vectors,” INF-05, “Near-patient diagnosis of the cause and treatability of most serious infections,” INF-06, “A dependable platform for generating new antibacterial treatments,” and INF-15, “A rapidly adaptable clinical phage-therapy platform,” are complementary infectious-disease capabilities. Their primary mechanisms—vector control, diagnosis, antibacterial development and phage therapy—remain separate from INF-08's pre-emptive vaccine breadth.

change_log.reason: These details explain the proposed challenge, but the retained source copies cannot substantiate the mechanisms.

change_log.reason: Both retained PubMed copies contain access notices rather than scientific content. Lack of verification is not evidence that the reported results are false.

change_log.change: Corrected the assertion that an earlier preprint abstract was available and its publication relationship established.
change_log.reason: The review found no abstract or bibliographic identity in the retained second artifact.

change_log.change: Integrated the distinction between isolated antibody activity, overall serum activity and durable protection.
change_log.reason: These are different evidentiary levels; a result at one level does not establish the others.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria into explicit proposals addressing endpoints, held-out viruses, reproducibility, durability and deployment.
change_log.reason: The original proposal left operational details unspecified and should not be mistaken for an established standard or proof of universal future coverage.

change_log.change: Qualified outbreak and population-level benefits and preserved the freshness limitation.
change_log.reason: Breadth alone does not establish transmission prevention, immediate population immunity, pandemic prevention or a complete account of the field through November 2026.

change_log.change: Used the supplied roster to clarify INF-09 and other conceptual relationships while keeping entries distinct.
change_log.reason: The roster permits a title-level comparison, resolving the review's concern about a wholly unavailable INF-09 definition only to that limited extent.

unresolved_issues: The reported Dueker study's identity, publication date, DOI and scientific findings remain unverified from the retained artifacts.
The second PubMed item's identity, alleged January 2026 preprint status and relationship to the reported publication remain unresolved.
Antibody rarity, cross-lineage neutralization, serum breadth and the reported absence of S2-directed serum cross-neutralization require inspectable scientific evidence.
The supplied material does not establish whether the target capability remains unachieved or whether research coverage is complete through 1 November 2026.
The intended coronavirus coverage, protection endpoints, durability period, target populations and acceptable performance thresholds remain unspecified.
A convincing held-out-virus panel and the relationship between its results, animal protection and human protection remain to be defined.
Related-concept comparisons are limited to the supplied roster titles; fuller definitions and evidence records were not provided.

brief.title: A vaccine against coronaviruses before they emerge
possible: People could enter a new coronavirus outbreak with protection already in place. A vaccine given beforehand would provide lasting protection even against substantially different viruses that were not used to design it.
why: Advance protection would give people a head start while a vaccine tailored to the new threat was developed. Protection against severe illness could ease pressure on hospitals. Protection against infection or spread could also help contain an outbreak.

sources.showed: Vaccinated macaques produced isolated antibodies, immune proteins that block viruses, active against distinct coronavirus groups. These protected animals against a test infection. Blood tests found no broad blocking activity targeting the shared region of the virus's surface protein.
sources.quote: These bnAbs neutralized diverse sarbeco- and merbecoviruses, including MERS-CoV, and conferred robust in vivo protection against SARS-CoV-2 challenge.
sources.cited_for: Vaccination can produce individual antibodies with activity across distinct coronavirus groups.
sources.not_established: Isolated protective antibodies do not establish that vaccination reliably produces lasting, broad protection in people.

sources.showed: An earlier version of the same work.

shown: Dueker and colleagues have demonstrated a protective ingredient in a macaque study. The remaining leap is for vaccination to produce enough broadly active antibodies throughout the immune response, keep them working over time, and protect against substantially different threats.
missing: Human trials still need to establish acceptable safety and lasting protection against multiple coronaviruses.
Protection must extend to diverse viruses excluded from vaccine design.
Independent teams must reproduce broad protection, with consistent responses across groups of recipients.
Manufacturing and delivery must support vaccination before an outbreak, including any repeat doses needed.

milestones.label: Human trials establish safety and lasting protection
milestones.explanation: Human trials would have to establish acceptable safety and lasting protection against multiple circulating coronaviruses, specifying which outcomes improve. This would establish a useful benefit for people.

milestones.label: Protection extends to viruses excluded from vaccine design
milestones.explanation: Laboratory tests and animal experiments would have to demonstrate protection against a diverse set of viruses chosen beforehand and excluded from vaccine design. This would test protection against unfamiliar threats.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce consistent protective responses
milestones.explanation: Independent laboratories would have to reproduce broad protection, while further groups of recipients show consistent, persistent responses. This would establish that success extends beyond exceptional individuals.

milestones.label: Manufacturing and delivery support vaccination before outbreaks
milestones.explanation: A feasible manufacturing and delivery programme would have to support advance vaccination, accounting for repeat doses and recipient limits. This would turn demonstrated protection into practical preparedness.

uncertain: The required virus coverage, duration of protection and acceptable level of benefit remain undefined.
Preventing severe illness, preventing infection and reducing spread are separate outcomes that need separate evidence.
How well tests against selected viruses predict human protection against future threats remains an open question.

page.title: Broadly protective betacoronavirus vaccine
page.definition: A vaccine given before exposure protects against severe disease for at least one year across sarbecoviruses and merbecoviruses—the coronavirus groups containing SARS and MERS viruses—including viruses whose antigens were absent from the vaccine.

goal.need: By June 2026, more than seven million confirmed COVID-19 deaths had been reported worldwide. A vaccine matched to a new virus can enter development only after the virus is identified. If a stockpiled vaccine protects against that virus and reaches people early, it could prevent severe illness and death while a matched vaccine is developed. A retrospective COVID-19 model estimated 54% fewer first-year deaths with an early stockpile sufficient to vaccinate 60% of people aged 60 or older. Protection against severe illness alone does not ensure that transmission stops.

completion.title: A vaccine receives a licence covering one-year protection across sarbecoviruses and merbecoviruses.
completion.criterion: A regulator licenses a vaccine for pre-exposure prevention of severe disease for at least one year after the specified regimen. The licensed indication covers viruses in both the sarbecovirus and merbecovirus subgenera. The regulator accepts evidence supporting protection against viruses whose antigens were absent from the vaccine, including pre-emergent animal viruses. Human safety data and the evidence of effectiveness required under the applicable licensing pathway support the indication.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis of CIDRAP’s product attributes and regulatory licensure. No regulator has defined a combined test for this breadth and duration.
completion.basis: CIDRAP specifies the two subgenera and at least one year of protection. Regulators consulted by CEPI considered even a pan-sarbecovirus indication insufficiently specific and advised that additional breadth data might be omitted from the label. Under the US Animal Rule, animal efficacy evidence may support approval with a bridge to humans if other pathways are infeasible and the rule’s requirements are met. The Atlas test specifies neither a panel size nor an efficacy percentage.

milestones.title: Vaccine-elicited antibodies neutralise a vaccine-absent coronavirus at the 50% assay endpoint.
milestones.criterion: Vaccine-elicited antibodies reduce viral entry by 50% in an assay against a coronavirus whose antigen was absent from the vaccine. Report the serum dilution or isolated-antibody concentration at that endpoint and identify which material was tested. The endpoint measures neutralisation in the assay.
milestones.set_by: Coronavirus neutralisation assay convention, illustrated by Cohen and colleagues in their 2021 study and in Figure 2 of their 2022 study.
milestones.threshold_quote: Half-maximal inhibitory dilutions (ID50 values) were determined

milestones.title: A coronavirus vaccine protects animals against challenge by a virus absent from its immunogens.
milestones.criterion: Compared with controls, vaccinated animals show protection after challenge with a coronavirus whose antigen was absent from the vaccine. Assess protection using the study’s prespecified endpoints, such as survival, weight loss and reduction in viral replication. The finding applies to the virus and animal model tested.
milestones.set_by: Animal-challenge convention in coronavirus vaccine research, applied in the Caltech/NIAID study by Cohen et al.; the cited experiment concerns sarbecoviruses.
milestones.threshold_quote: evaluate survival, weight loss, and reduction or absence of viral replication as the primary metrics for vaccine efficacy

milestones.title: A volunteer receives the candidate vaccine under an effective US Investigational New Drug application.
milestones.criterion: At least one participant receives the candidate vaccine under the clinical protocol after the Investigational New Drug application takes effect. The application takes effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA imposes a clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigation may begin.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.40(b) and (d).
milestones.threshold_quote: An investigator may not administer an investigational new drug to human subjects until the IND goes into effect

milestones.title: A phase 1 vaccine study assesses safety and detects neutralisation of a sarbecovirus beyond SARS-CoV-2.
milestones.criterion: A phase 1 study completes its protocol-defined safety and immune-response assessments. Serum from vaccinated participants shows detectable neutralisation of at least one sarbecovirus other than SARS-CoV-2. In the SpFN/ALFQ protocol, the primary antibody assessment was on day 43 (±2 days). The trial publication reports cross-sarbecovirus neutralisation as an additional measurement.
milestones.set_by: US Army Medical Research and Development Command, protocol NCT04784767, for the phase 1 assessments. The breadth measurement follows the published SpFN/ALFQ study.
milestones.threshold_quote: Number of participants with humoral immune response at Study Day 43 (+/- 2).

milestones.title: A coronavirus vaccine completes controlled phase 2 safety and dose–response assessment.
milestones.criterion: A randomised, controlled phase 2 study completes its comparison of vaccine doses in participants relevant to the intended use. It assesses common short-term adverse effects and measures how immune response varies with dose using standardised, validated tests.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Vaccine Development – 101, phase 2 development stage.
milestones.threshold_quote: examine the relationship between the dose administered and the immune response

milestones.title: The manufacturer submits a US licence application for the proposed breadth and duration of protection.
milestones.criterion: The manufacturer submits a Biologics License Application to FDA for the proposed indication. The application includes the preclinical and clinical evidence required for that licensing pathway and information on the commercial manufacturing process and facilities. It supports the proposed duration of protection and identifies the viruses covered by the claim.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, The Path for Vaccines from Research to FDA Approval.
milestones.threshold_quote: the manufacturer submits a BLA to the FDA.

milestones.title: A vaccine demonstrates clinical proof of concept across the virus panel for its intended use.
milestones.criterion: Phase 1/2 studies demonstrate safety in the intended population. A high proportion of recipients have robust neutralising titres against a virus panel appropriate to the target product profile, supported by other immune measurements. The clinical evidence warrants late-stage development. CEPI gives 80% or more of recipients as an example responder proportion. It specifies neither a universal titre nor a clinical efficacy percentage.
milestones.set_by: Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, provisional clinical proof-of-concept criteria in section 2.2 of its 2021 call for proposals.
milestones.threshold_quote: Robust neutralization titers in a high proportion of vaccinees (e.g. 80% or more)

not_found: No integrated external completion test specifying a pre-emergent coronavirus panel, clinical efficacy threshold and duration of protection was located.
No published pivotal human efficacy result supporting protection across sarbecoviruses and merbecoviruses was located.
The publisher’s full text of the 2026 Cell Reports paper by Dueker and colleagues could not be opened.

results.finding: Two isolated macaque monoclonal antibodies cross-neutralized sarbecoviruses and merbecoviruses. The macaque sample size was unreported.
results.detail: MERS-CoV is the only neutralized virus named in the text, and its spike was used as a booster.
results.quote: These bnAbs neutralized diverse sarbeco- and merbecoviruses, including MERS-CoV, and conferred robust in vivo protection against SARS-CoV-2 challenge.

results.finding: Two vaccine-elicited monoclonal antibodies conferred protection against SARS-CoV-2 challenge. The challenge-group sample size was unreported.
results.detail: The supplied text leaves the challenge animal model unspecified.
results.quote: These bnAbs neutralized diverse sarbeco- and merbecoviruses, including MERS-CoV, and conferred robust in vivo protection against SARS-CoV-2 challenge.

results.finding: Serum from 8 vaccinated macaques neutralized vaccine-absent sarbecoviruses at the 50% assay endpoint.
results.detail: The numerical IC50 stated in the prose is for SARS-CoV-2, whose spike was included in the vaccine.
results.quote: the high titers of cross-neutralizing antibody responses against diverse sarbecoviruses (SARS-CoV-1, WIV1, and Pang17) were durable and persisted for more than six months (week 38) post the SARS-CoV-2 spike boost (week 10)

results.finding: Mice given CHM-16 (n=9) or CHM-27 (n=8) lost less weight after SARS-CoV-2 challenge than controls (n=11, P<0.0001).
results.quote: The S2 stem-helix bnAb treated animals showed significantly reduced weight loss as compared to the negative control antibody SMZAb1-treated animals at day 6 (P<0.0001,

results.finding: Trivalent RBD nanoparticle vaccine serum (8 mice per group) neutralised SARS-CoV pseudovirus at a geometric mean 50% endpoint dilution of about 1:1,000–1:2,000.
results.quote: Strikingly, the trivalent nanoparticle immunogens (mRBD-NP-DO and cRBD-NP-DO)—which did not contain the SARS-CoV RBD—also elicited potent neutralization (GMT ∼1–2 × 10 3 ).

results.finding: After SARS-CoV MA15 challenge, all 8 mice given the mosaic vaccine lacking SARS-CoV RBD had undetectable lung virus.
results.detail: The lung plaque assay detection limit was 90 PFU per lobe. Unvaccinated controls reached approximately 1 million PFU per lobe.
results.quote: mRBD-NP- and mRBD-NP-DO-vaccinated mice were completely protected from viral replication in the lungs ( Figure 6 C).

results.finding: Serum from eight mosaic-8b-vaccinated macaques neutralised vaccine-absent SARS-CoV in a 50% endpoint assay.
results.detail: Figure 4 reports the endpoint dilutions. The prose cites a 1:100 benchmark for SARS-CoV-2 variant responses and gives no numerical dilution for SARS-CoV.

results.finding: After vaccine-absent SARS-CoV challenge, 6/6 K18-hACE2 mice per mosaic vaccine group survived.
results.detail: Ten mice per group were challenged. Six were followed for survival and four were assessed for viral load. In the macaque SARS-CoV comparison, infectious virus was undetectable in all four vaccinated animals, but the group differences did not reach statistical significance.
results.quote: all mice in the mosaic-8b and mosaic-8 g group survived the challenge during the 28 days of post-challenge monitoring

results.finding: The completed US phase 1 SpFN/ALFQ trial enrolled 29 participants.
results.detail: The registry lists the vaccine and placebo schedules as planned and provides no participant dosing results.

results.finding: Vaccinated aged-mouse serum had a WIV-1 neutralising titre 1.2 times its SARS-CoV-2 titre. Sample size unreported in the supplied text.
results.quote: Last, mice in group 1 generated the most balanced and highest neutralizing titers, which were 13- and 1.2-fold increased against SARS-CoV and WIV-1 and less than onefold decreased against RsSHC014 relative to the SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing titers

results.finding: Aged mice in 2 chimeric mRNA vaccine groups were fully protected against WIV-1 challenge. Sample size unreported in the supplied text.
results.quote: Mice from groups 1 and 2 were fully protected against heterologous WIV-1 challenge, whereas mice that received the SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccine had breakthrough replication in the lung

results.finding: Mosaic-8b macaque sera (n = 8 vaccinated) reached the 50% entry-inhibition endpoint against SARS-CoV pseudovirus.
results.detail: The supplied Figure 4 caption defines the endpoint as ID50. The individual titers are plotted in the figure, and the supplied text contains only the caption.
results.quote: neutralized in pseudovirus assays for human ACE2 entry-dependent viral strains for which neutralization assays could be conducted including mismatched strains: SARS-1

results.finding: Mosaic-8b K18-hACE2 mice (n = 6 monitored per arm) had 100% survival after SARS-CoV challenge.
results.detail: Each mouse challenge arm included 10 animals, with 6 monitored for survival and 4 sampled for virology. Macaque challenge outcomes were based on viral load.
results.quote: whereas all mice in the mosaic-8b and mosaic-8 g group survived the challenge during the 28 days of post-challenge monitoring

results.finding: SpFN/ALFQ phase 1 trial: 24 of 29 randomized adults received at least one dose of the candidate vaccine.
results.detail: The paper gives neither an FDA receipt date from which to assess the 30-day period nor an FDA notice allowing the trial to begin earlier.
results.quote: Overall, 88% (n=21/24) of participants who received the vaccine reported one or more solicited AEs of any kind following either the first, second or third dose.

results.finding: At day 43, serum from all 9 SpFN/ALFQ recipients in the cross-neutralisation analysis neutralised RaTG13 pseudovirus.
results.detail: The cross-neutralisation analysis shown in Figure 4F used samples from the 25 µg recipients who later took the optional third dose.
results.quote: Neutralizing antibody responses at day 43 were robust in all participants against RaTG13, the virus most closely related to SARS-CoV-2.

results.finding: Post-vaccination serum from 22 older adults reached the 50% entry-neutralisation endpoint against BANAL-20-52 spike pseudovirus at a geometric mean dilution of 1:16,063.
results.detail: The assay measured entry of spike-pseudotyped lentivirus into HEK293T cells expressing human ACE2. Participants had mixed SARS-CoV-2 infection histories, so the study could not isolate the vaccine's contribution to each serum titre.
results.quote:
Yet rather surprisingly, BANAL-20-52 and pangolin CoV were
neutralised signiﬁcantly better than Wu-1, with NT50 values approximately
7.4-fold and 13.3-fold higher than that of Wu-1 (GMT = 16063 and 29018,
respectively, compared to 2180)

results.finding: NL140422 spike-vaccinated hDPP4 mice (n=5 per group) had 2.5-log lower lung viral titers than controls after MERS-CoV challenge.
results.detail: The HKU4 spike vaccine also reduced lung viral titers by 1.7 log units. Neither vaccine significantly reduced nasal turbinate titers. The study did not report survival or weight-loss efficacy outcomes.
results.quote:
Mice immunized with VLP -NL140422 S and VLP-HKU4 S
demonstrated partial cross-protection against MERS-CoV, showing 2.5 and
1.7 log reductions in lung viral titers compared to the control group,
respectively.

goal.need = "By June 2026, more than seven million confirmed COVID-19 deaths had been reported worldwide. A vaccine matched to a new virus can enter development only after the virus is identified. If a stockpiled vaccine protects against that virus and reaches people early, it could prevent severe illness and death while a matched vaccine is developed. A retrospective COVID-19 model estimated 54% fewer first-year deaths with an early stockpile sufficient to vaccinate 60% of people aged 60 or older. Protection against severe illness alone does not ensure that transmission stops.". Reason: The current paragraph counts outbreaks but omits the human toll and the interval during which a stockpiled vaccine could protect people.

add statement by WHO coronavirus Collaborative Open Research Consortium, 2026: "Develop pan-sarbecovirus/merbecovirus vaccines based on humoral (B-cell)/cell mediated (T-cell) immunity.". Reason: The 2026 roadmap explicitly names both subgenera in a single vaccine development objective.

edit completion: criterion = "A regulator licenses a vaccine for pre-exposure prevention of severe disease for at least one year after the specified regimen. The licensed indication covers viruses in both the sarbecovirus and merbecovirus subgenera. The regulator accepts evidence supporting protection against viruses whose antigens were absent from the vaccine, including pre-emergent animal viruses. Human safety data and the evidence of effectiveness required under the applicable licensing pathway support the indication."; set_by = "Atlas synthesis of CIDRAP\u2019s product attributes and regulatory licensure. No regulator has defined a combined test for this breadth and duration."; set_by_kind = "atlas"; basis = "CIDRAP specifies the two subgenera and at least one year of protection. Regulators consulted by CEPI considered even a pan-sarbecovirus indication insufficiently specific and advised that additional breadth data might be omitted from the label. Under the US Animal Rule, animal efficacy evidence may support approval with a bridge to humans if other pathways are infeasible and the rule\u2019s requirements are met. The Atlas test specifies neither a panel size nor an efficacy percentage."; refs = [1, 5, 6, 10, 18]. Reason: The existing test omits the regulatory objection to an unspecified breadth claim and implies that direct human efficacy evidence is required under every licensing pathway.

edit m1: criterion = "Vaccine-elicited antibodies reduce viral entry by 50% in an assay against a coronavirus whose antigen was absent from the vaccine. Report the serum dilution or isolated-antibody concentration at that endpoint and identify which material was tested. The endpoint measures neutralisation in the assay."; set_by = "Coronavirus neutralisation assay convention, illustrated by Cohen and colleagues in their 2021 study and in Figure 2 of their 2022 study."; set_by_kind = "community_convention"; threshold_quote = "Half-maximal inhibitory dilutions (ID50 values) were determined"; threshold_ref = 20; refs = [9, 20]. Reason: The revision supplies the missing source for the 50% endpoint and separates the assay result from evidence of protection.

edit m2: criterion = "Compared with controls, vaccinated animals show protection after challenge with a coronavirus whose antigen was absent from the vaccine. Assess protection using the study\u2019s prespecified endpoints, such as survival, weight loss and reduction in viral replication. The finding applies to the virus and animal model tested."; threshold_quote = "evaluate survival, weight loss, and reduction or absence of viral replication as the primary metrics for vaccine efficacy"; threshold_ref = 9; refs = [9]. Reason: The existing criterion embeds one mouse cohort’s survival result in a test intended to apply to other candidates.

edit m3: title = "A volunteer receives the candidate vaccine under an effective US Investigational New Drug application."; criterion = "At least one participant receives the candidate vaccine under the clinical protocol after the Investigational New Drug application takes effect. The application takes effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA imposes a clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigation may begin."; set_by = "US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.40(b) and (d)."; set_by_kind = "regulator"; threshold_quote = "An investigator may not administer an investigational new drug to human subjects until the IND goes into effect"; threshold_ref = 22; refs = [22, 10]. Reason: The regulation defines when an IND takes effect, whereas the current title suggests a separate affirmative approval and the criterion includes one trial’s enrolment.

edit m4: title = "A phase 1 vaccine study assesses safety and detects neutralisation of a sarbecovirus beyond SARS-CoV-2."; criterion = "A phase 1 study completes its protocol-defined safety and immune-response assessments. Serum from vaccinated participants shows detectable neutralisation of at least one sarbecovirus other than SARS-CoV-2. In the SpFN/ALFQ protocol, the primary antibody assessment was on day 43 (\u00b12 days). The trial publication reports cross-sarbecovirus neutralisation as an additional measurement."; set_by = "US Army Medical Research and Development Command, protocol NCT04784767, for the phase 1 assessments. The breadth measurement follows the published SpFN/ALFQ study."; set_by_kind = "protocol"; threshold_quote = "Number of participants with humoral immune response at Study Day 43 (+/- 2)."; threshold_ref = 23; refs = [23, 11]. Reason: The revision distinguishes the registered immune-response endpoint from the additional breadth measurement and removes the trial’s outcomes from the criterion.

edit m5: criterion = "A randomised, controlled phase 2 study completes its comparison of vaccine doses in participants relevant to the intended use. It assesses common short-term adverse effects and measures how immune response varies with dose using standardised, validated tests."; threshold_quote = "examine the relationship between the dose administered and the immune response"; threshold_ref = 10; refs = [10]. Reason: A portfolio listing for a combined phase I/II trial does not define completion of phase 2 dose assessment.

add milestone after m5: "A vaccine demonstrates clinical proof of concept across the virus panel for its intended use.". Reason: CEPI defines a human proof-of-concept test for breadth that a dose-ranging study alone need not meet.

edit m6: title = "The manufacturer submits a US licence application for the proposed breadth and duration of protection."; criterion = "The manufacturer submits a Biologics License Application to FDA for the proposed indication. The application includes the preclinical and clinical evidence required for that licensing pathway and information on the commercial manufacturing process and facilities. It supports the proposed duration of protection and identifies the viruses covered by the claim."; set_by = "US Food and Drug Administration, The Path for Vaccines from Research to FDA Approval."; set_by_kind = "regulator"; threshold_quote = "the manufacturer submits a BLA to the FDA."; threshold_ref = 5; refs = [5, 10, 1]. Reason: Submission of the licence application is the single, verifiable event that brings the pivotal evidence and commercial manufacturing process together for FDA review.
